newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuania c. bank says aims at stable currency, EU.
newsitem.headline: Lithuania c. bank says aims at stable currency, EU.

text.p: Lithuania's central bank on Thursday said its new monetary policy would keep the litas currency stable and further the country's integration with Europe.
The central bank earlier said that it would seek to reassert control over monetary policy by ending the present currency board system regulating the litas.
But it stressed that the peg of four litas to one dollar would be maintained despite the changes. Many feared that an end to the currency board would lead to a litas devaluation.

"...the Bank of Lithuania takes on the duty to keep the fixed currency exchange rate regime and the change to the litas reliability law (regulating the currency) will not have a big influence on financial markets," the bank said in a statement.
"There will also be the chance effectively to regulate the liquidity of the bank system. The Bank of Lithuania will have the chance to use modern monetary policy means."
